title: Seattle Central Library
visualBrief: The 2004 OMA/LMN Central Library on the block between Fourth and Fifth Avenues, Madison and Spring Streets: a stack of shifted platforms wrapped in one faceted skin of glass under a light diamond steel grid. Two-storey storefront and a covered plaza under the cantilevered meeting platform on Fourth Avenue, the sloping living-room roof falling to Fifth Avenue, the books-spiral box cantilevered over Spring Street, the reading-room slopes, and the headquarters platform cantilevered over Fifth Avenue and Madison Street, with the core penthouse on the roof.
scaleBasis: Measured: plan from the mapped footprint in footprint.json, heights from the sourced dimensions below.
geometrySource: Original deterministic Molen mesh generator models/generate-seattle-central-library.mjs; no third-party model or bitmap texture.

dimensions.fact: Plan: the mapped OSM building 35184409145274 (the block outline, with its chamfered corners) and its roof parts 35184830292122/26/28/31, which show the flat headquarters roof and the reading-room slopes toward Spring Street, Fourth Avenue and Madison Street

11 storeys, 185 ft (56.4 m) to the roof, 362,987 sq ft; address 1000 Fourth Avenue on the block bounded by Fourth and Fifth Avenues and Madison and Spring Streets; level 1 faces Fourth Avenue, level 3 faces Fifth Avenue

Diamond grid 4 ft wide by 7 ft tall (4 ft on a side); nearly 10,000 diamonds over about 130,000 sq ft of curtain wall; platforms from bottom to top: staff, living room, meeting, mixing chamber, four-level books platform, reading room, one-storey headquarters cantilevering up to 28 ft; 213 ft concrete core in the southwest quadrant

Diamonds 7 ft tall at their tallest and 4 ft wide at their widest; the Fourth Avenue entrance sits beneath a large cantilevered section; the grade change between the entrances fits a staff level between the two public floors
Platforms cantilever up to 52 ft; a diamond steel grid ties the platform trusses together and carries the curtain wall
Level 3 living room along Fifth Avenue reaches 50 ft in height; Books Spiral on levels 6 through 9

appearance.colorEncoding: sRGB palette decoded to linear COLOR_0

limitations: Platform heights and plan offsets are read from street photographs (the Fifth Avenue elevation and the views from Fourth and Madison and Fifth and Spring) and the mapped roof parts; they are estimates, not survey levels.

Every skin plane spans straight between two platform edges, so the folds are simplified: the V-shaped plane under the books platform at Fourth and Madison, the sloped columns at the Fifth and Spring corner and the headquarters bevel toward Madison Street are approximations.
Glass is clear, mesh-laminated (light) or seen from below per plane; the scattered opaque diamonds and the interior (red floor, yellow escalators, books spiral) are not modelled.

The explorer terrain has a 5-9 m pit over this block that reaches about 25 m east of Fifth Avenue, so the level 3 Fifth Avenue entrance (modelled at real grade, 9.3 m above Fourth Avenue) can stand above the drawn street there.

Original deterministic geometry from mapped footprints, published dimensions and general knowledge of the building; not a survey, photogrammetric reconstruction or replica of any third-party model. No photographs or generated bitmaps are embedded.
